title: Proximity-weighted ejection and throughput-aware routing policy
creator: Priya Desai
description: Implement a routing policy that combines proximity-weighted scoring (favoring lower-latency regions) with throughput-aware ejection (temporarily removing or de-weighting regions experiencing GPU saturation or local congestion). The policy should tie into SLO monitoring and circuit-breaker state to provide graceful degradation and controlled load shedding rather than hard failures. This ticket covers the design, prototype, tests, and a staged rollout for the policy across hosted and dedicated environments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller can compute a region score per request using a weighted combination of latency percentile (p50/p95), recent throughput/GPU utilization, and sticky-affinity hints.
2) When a region score falls below threshold the controller will place the region into a graduated ejection state (soft-degrade -> limited -> ejected) instead of immediate blackhole.
3) Circuit-breaker transitions (closed/half-open/open) are correlated with ejection states and surfaced in Console.
4) Canary rollout across two non-critical customers without SLO regressions; telemetry shows no client-visible error spikes.
5) Automated chaos test demonstrating fallback to secondary regions within SLO budget for 95% of requests.
6) Documentation and playbook for on-call mitigation and post-incident recovery exist in Confluence.
technical_design:
Overview: Replace the current binary geo-pin/pin-fallback logic with a continuous scoring function: score = w1 * latency_component + w2 * capacity_component + w3 * affinity_bonus.
Latency_component: derived from sliding-window p50/p95 normalized to 0..1. Capacity_component: sigmoid-scaled function of GPU utilization, queue length, and drop-rate. Affinity_bonus: positive bias for requests with prefix pinning or KV-cache hotness.
Ejection states:
- Soft-degrade: reduce incoming weight by 30% and enable per-request hedging.
- Throttled: apply 429 backpressure for low-priority requests and enforce per-tenant mini-queues.
- Ejected: mark region as unavailable for new requests for a short cool-down with periodic half-open probes.
Circuit Breakers: Use a token-leaky window measuring error rate and latency; transitions bump ejection state. Half-open probes use small sampled traffic routed with additional tracing.
Routing flow changes: controller computes scores at decision time, caches recent scores per region (10s TTL) and serves decisions from local cache to avoid coordinator hot paths. The agent will support both global and per-customer overrides.
Data plane impact: batching and prefix caching will be preserved; when a region is ejected, KV cache miss rates may rise—policy will trigger a warm-up window that sends a small subset of traffic to the ejected region to prime caches before returning full load.
Telemetry: New metrics (region_score, ejection_state, probe_success_rate, per-region_gpus_utilization) exported. Console will show per-route breakdown with sliders to simulate weight adjustments.
Compatibility: Works with Dedicated (maps to pool IDs) and Hosted (maps to region names). Falls back to existing fallback chains when topology doesn't support partial ejection.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag gated: default off for tenants.
2) Unit tests + integration tests in dev environment.
3) Canary: enable for internal infra tenants and two low-traffic external customers for 48h with increased telemetry collection.
4) Monitor SLO windows (latency p95 and error-rate) and rollback if >5% regression in SLO breach rate.
5) Expand to 20% of traffic in region batches over 7 days with automated abort on SLA regressions.
6) Turn on for all hosted traffic, then expose controls to Dedicated customers for opt-in.
7) Post-rollout: 30-day observation and tuning sprint for policy weights and thresholds.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests for scoring math and ejection state transitions.
- Integration test harness simulating multi-region capacity loss, verifying fallback timing and cache warm-up behavior.
- Load test: inject queue saturation and validate that throughput-aware ejection prevents tail latency amplification.
- Chaos test: terminate 1 region's serving pool and ensure at least 95% of requests meet SLO after failover.
- Observability smoke tests for metrics and traces in Console.
- Canary success criteria: no more than 1.5x baseline rate of retries or user-visible 500s for canary tenants.
metrics_and_alerting:
Primary metrics: region_score (gauge), ejection_state (enum), per_region_gpu_utilization (gauge), request_success_rate (percentage), p95_latency_by_region (ms), cache_miss_rate (percent).
Alerts:
- region_score < 0.25 for >30s -> page on-call (potential partial outage).
- probe_success_rate < 50% during half-open -> escalate.
- downstream_error_rate increase >2x baseline -> fire annotatable incident in PagerDuty.
Dashboards: Per-route heatmap showing active ejection states and traffic weights; historical correlation view between utilization spikes and ejection events.
